question: Explain requirement review.
answerMd:
### University Examination Solution: Requirements Engineering (SE Unit 3) #### Question: > **Explain requirement review.** > *[1 Mark | MGIT CSE Semester III | Source Paper: jan 2026.pdf Q1(f)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rfbaesWw8UcfQDP7ey4zsxzErd6M-MVA/view)* --- ### 1. Direct Exam Definition (1 Mark) A **Requirements Review** is a structured, formal inspection of the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document conducted collaboratively by developers, clients, system end-users, and domain experts to uncover ambiguities, omissions, inconsistencies, and inaccuracies before advancing to system design and implementation. **Primary Objectives:** - **Defect Detection:** Catch errors in requirements early when the cost of repair is lowest (Boehm's cost-of-change curve). - **Quality Verification:** Validate completeness, consistency, feasibility, testability, and traceability. - **Stakeholder Consensus:** Ensure developers and clients share an unambiguous, identical understanding of contractual obligations. ---
Learn more: Extended Inspection Workflow & Team Roles (Full Breakdown) ### 2. Formal Inspection Process & Team Roles Formal requirements reviews (e.g., Fagan Inspections) establish structured roles: 1. **Moderator (Chair):** Leads the review session, ensures adherence to agenda, and maintains objectivity. 2. **Author (Analyst):** The requirements engineer who drafted the specification; clarifies intent but does not defend defects. 3. **Reader:** Paraphrases the specification line-by-line during the review meeting. 4. **Inspectors / Reviewers:** Stakeholders who scrutinize requirements against standard checklists. 5. **Scribe (Recorder):** Documents all logged ambiguities and action items. ### 3. Review Checklist Criteria - **Completeness:** Are all functional capabilities, performance constraints, and external interfaces documented? - **Consistency:** Are there conflicting constraints or contradictory requirements between sections? - **Feasibility:** Can the requirements be realized within technology, budget, and schedule limits? - **Verifiability (Testability):** Can each requirement be objectively tested with a measurable pass/fail criterion? - **Traceability:** Is each requirement uniquely identified and mapped to customer goals? ### 4. Review Lifecycle Phases `Planning → Overview → Individual Preparation → Inspection Meeting → Rework → Follow-up`
